what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat HIV-1 infection in adults and children who weigh at least 35 kg (about 77 pounds). It contains three HIV medicines in one pill that work together to lower the amount of HIV virus in your blood. This helps keep your immune system stronger and lowers your chance of getting infections or illnesses caused by HIV. This medicine does NOT cure HIV, but it helps control it.
how_to_take: Take ONE tablet by mouth ONCE daily WITH a full meal (not just a snack). The food helps your body absorb the medicine properly. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, chew, or split it. Try to take it at the same time every day to keep the drug levels steady in your body.
dosing: The usual dose for adults and children weighing at least 35 kg is ONE tablet once daily with food. Do not take more or less than prescribed. Your doctor will decide if this dose is right for you based on your weight, kidney function, and other medicines you take.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been LESS than 12 hours since your scheduled time, take it right away with food. If it has been MORE than 12 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time with food. NEVER take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Missing doses can allow the virus to become harder to treat (drug resistance), so try your best not to miss any.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Protect from light and moisture. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Do not use if the expiration date on the bottle has passed.
what_to_avoid: Do not take antacids, calcium supplements, iron supplements, or multivitamins within 2 hours before or 4 hours after taking this medicine, as they can make it less effective. Avoid the following medicines while taking this drug — they can cause serious problems: rifampin, rifabutin, rifapentine, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, St. John's Wort (herbal supplement), proton pump inhibitors like omeprazole or pantoprazole, and dexamethasone (more than one dose). Always tell every doctor, dentist, and pharmacist about ALL medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take. Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol, as it can stress your liver.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you experience: severe stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting that does not stop; yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice); dark-colored urine or pale stools; fast or irregular heartbeat; muscle pain, weakness, or cramping; difficulty breathing; severe rash or skin blistering; mood changes, depression, thoughts of self-harm, or unusual sadness; signs of a kidney problem such as decreased urination or swelling in your legs or feet; or any new or worsening symptoms after starting the medicine. Some patients experience a reaction called 'immune reconstitution syndrome' early in treatment, where the immune system starts fighting old hidden infections — tell your doctor if you develop any new symptoms after starting.
when_it_works: This medicine starts working right away after you begin taking it, but it may take several weeks to months before your viral load (the amount of HIV in your blood) drops to very low or undetectable levels. Most people start to see improvements in lab results within 4 to 8 weeks. You will need regular blood tests to check how well the medicine is working and to monitor your kidneys, liver, and bone health. Even when you feel well and your viral load is undetectable, keep taking your medicine every day — stopping can cause the virus to come back stronger.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor immediately if you become pregnant or plan to become pregnant. HIV medicines during pregnancy can reduce the risk of passing HIV to your baby, but your doctor may need to adjust your treatment. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine, as HIV can be passed to your baby through breast milk. Kidney problems: This medicine may not be safe if you have moderate to severe kidney disease. Your doctor will check your kidney function before and during treatment. Older adults: Use with caution — older patients may have reduced kidney function that requires monitoring. Children: Only approved for children weighing at least 35 kg (about 77 pounds). Not recommended for infants or toddlers.
